scope: A fixed synthetic two-state, 12-generation Feynman-Kac particle-filter stress test with one discrete shock position, total cost 768 particle-steps, 2,500 independent repetitions per each of 12 shock positions, seed 202608281905, and the explicitly specified 192-cost pilot plus 576-cost production allocation. Within this exact experiment, the reusable-pilot design's MSE ratio versus full-uniform has reported mean 1.027991, minimum 0.779635 and maximum 1.170099; discarding the paid pilot has reported mean ratio 1.340587. This supports the narrow negative conclusion that the tested generation-local raw-potential-CV^2 allocation is not a robust MSE improvement over full uniform in this stress. It does not establish universal failure or superiority of adaptive allocation, any theorem about other models/shock regimes, or real-agent/AGI performance.

phase1_acceptance_boundary: This candidate contributes a narrow negative guard: local raw-potential CV^2 alone is not shown robustly superior under the exact synthetic stress and should not be promoted as a generic dependency-elimination mechanism. It does not close any end-to-end Work-dependency-elimination row or the Phase-1 root. All accepted routes still require zero residual execution dependency, zero finite quota dependency, zero incremental cost, useful outcome parity, conflict/authority safety, zero-quota/rate-limit replay and scheduler persistence.
